topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the opening welcome and contextual framing for the lecture on complement.

topics.label: Overview, nomenclature, and the central role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics introduce the general principles, naming conventions, and central activating role of C3 in the complement cascade.

topics.label: Complement activation pathways and threshold
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the three biochemical pathways that recognize pathogens and converge to generate convertases and trigger complement activation.

topics.label: Effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the downstream processes by which activated complement eliminates pathogens through opsonization, inflammation, and membrane lysis.

topics.label: Host regulation of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines the regulatory proteins that protect host cells from accidental complement-mediated destruction.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic discusses the distinct medical presentations and pathologies associated with genetic or acquired deficiencies in complement components.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion mechanisms
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explores how pathogens, particularly Staphylococcus aureus, evade and neutralize host complement defenses.

topics.label: Lecture closing
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic concludes the lecture and previews the upcoming session on the adaptive immune system.
